name: banknifty_lead_lag_5s
author: adapted from quant_system
thesis: Bank NIFTY leads NIFTY 50 by 1-5 minutes during directional moves because banking stocks are the highest-weight sector and institutional flows hit banks first. When Bank NIFTY makes a sharp move but NIFTY laggards haven't caught up, there's a window to trade the laggards. The inefficiency exists due to differential liquidity across NIFTY constituents — banks trade faster, IT/pharma lag. Not fully arbitraged because the lead-lag window is narrow (1-5 min) and requires pre-computed signals and fast execution.
mechanism: BANK NIFTY carries ~33% weight in NIFTY 50, creating tight but imperfect correlation. Temporary spread dislocations arise from sector-specific order flow (banking-focused FII buying, RBI policy expectations, credit events). These dislocations mean-revert as index arbitrageurs and ETF creation/redemption mechanisms force the relationship back to equilibrium.

indicators.name: lag_signal
indicators.purpose: how much the stock is lagging Bank NIFTY

weaknesses: Lead-lag relationships are not stable — the 'leader' changes based on what's driving the market that day. Bank NIFTY doesn't always lead.
Small per-trade edge (20 bps) with high frequency means costs eat a huge chunk. Any slippage increase destroys profitability.
The 1-5 minute window is extremely tight for Zerodha execution. Co-location traders with DMA will eat this edge before retail can act.
prior_art: Lead-lag pairs trading. See: Algorithmic Trading (Chan), Advances in Financial Machine Learning (de Prado) on lead-lag estimation.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to BANKNIFTY index.
